regime.headline: Dovish repricing
regime.paragraph: Rates markets priced a more dovish policy path: US Treasury yields 2Y -5bp to 4.58% and 10Y -8bp to 4.89%. The US curve saw a bull flattener in 2s10s (-2bp to 31bp). The dollar fell 0.3%, gold rose 3.4%, the S&P 500 rose 1.6% and Brent fell 9.2%. US high-yield spreads tightened 3bp. The standout move was WTI crude (-9.0%, 3.5x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries rallied with the long end leading, 2Y -5bp to 4.58% and 10Y -8bp to 4.89%: a bull flattener (2s10s -2bp). Markets removed 5bp of Fed tightening over 12 months (now +53bp). The dollar fell 0.3% and the S&P 500 rose 1.6%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts rallied, 2Y -12bp to 4.74% and 10Y -13bp to 5.13%: a bull flattener (2s10s -1bp). Gilts outperformed Treasuries by 5bp at 10Y. Markets added 6bp of BoE tightening over 12 months (now +107bp). Sterling rose 0.4% and the FTSE 100 rose 1.8%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds rallied with the long end leading, 2Y -1bp to 3.01% and 10Y -2bp to 3.29%: a bull flattener (2s10s -2bp). BTP-Bund tightened 11bp to 103bp. ECB pricing was steady at +58bp over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy. The euro rose 0.3% and the Euro Stoxx 50 rose 2.0%.

regions.name: Japan
regions.text: JGB 10Y yields rose 4bp to 2.807%, with 30Y +5bp. The yen strengthened as USD/JPY moved -0.1% to 158.44. BoJ pricing was steady at +92bp over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy. The Nikkei fell 1.7%.

regions.name: China
regions.text: CGB 10Y yields fell 1bp to 1.60%. The renminbi weakened with USD/CNY +0.04% at 6.6735. The CSI 300 rose 2.3% and copper rose 0.1%.

relationships.statement: Lower oil pulled US breakevens down.
relationships.lesson: Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

relationships.statement: Gold rose despite higher real yields.
relationships.lesson: Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

relationships.statement: Tighter BTP–Bund spreads signalled stronger demand for periphery risk.
relationships.lesson: BTP–Bund is the euro area's main gauge of sovereign and fragmentation risk; it usually widens with risk-off and narrows when risk appetite is strong.

relationships.statement: Gilts outperformed Bunds, pointing to UK-specific relief from data, BoE pricing or fiscal news.
relationships.lesson: Cross-market spreads strip out the global rates move, isolating what was local.

relationships.statement: Lower US yields weighed on the dollar.
relationships.lesson: Higher US yields raise the return on dollar assets and attract capital. When the dollar moves against yields, risk sentiment or non-US news is usually driving FX instead.

relationships.statement: Narrower Treasury–Bund spreads favoured EUR over USD.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

relationships.statement: A long-end-led rally flattened the Treasury curve, consistent with growth concerns or demand for duration.
relationships.lesson: Long-end yields fell more than the front end: a growth scare, lower inflation risk or duration demand.

interview.question: Why did BTP–Bund spreads tighten?
interview.answer: BTP–Bund moved -11bp to 103bp. The spread prices Italian sovereign credit and redenomination risk relative to Germany. It widens with global risk-off, Italian fiscal or political news, or a hawkish ECB (higher rates raise debt-servicing concerns), and tightens with strong risk appetite and carry demand. The ECB's TPI backstop limits disorderly widening. Today's Euro Stoxx move was +2.0%.

interview.question: Why did Gilts outperform Bunds?
interview.answer: 10Y Gilts moved -13bp versus -2bp for Bunds, so the spread moved -11bp to 185bp (61th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Why did Bunds outperform JGBs?
interview.answer: 10Y JGBs moved +4bp versus -2bp for Bunds, so the spread moved +6bp to -48bp (64th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Bank of England, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 3.75%. Markets price a 95% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 4.3 hikes (107bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.85%. The 12-month pricing moved +6bp on the day. Method: Bank of England SONIA OIS curve. Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +107bp is 4.3 moves.

interview.question: Was today's Treasury rally driven by real yields or inflation expectations?
interview.answer: Nominal yields fell 7.7bp, driven by both real yields and inflation expectations (real +3.0bp, breakeven -4.0bp). Nominal yield = real yield + breakeven inflation. Real-yield-led moves usually reflect policy expectations or growth; breakeven-led moves reflect inflation risk, often energy prices. Brent moved -9.2%.

What was today's largest volatility-adjusted move?

flashcards.back: Yields rise with the long end rising more than the front. Usually term premium, fiscal supply or inflation risk, not a policy repricing.
